about: Pinned F2 differential seeds for CI (W7c): the summaries this revision of forge-blend produces (W6 review round 6). THE F2 GATE STILL FAILS ON BOTH SEEDS (each seed's `gate` lists why): Forge's validity is below OCCT's (552 < 580, 549 < 582), MATCH + NORMALIZED is below 99 % (95.9 %, 96.1 %), and Forge bodies without an independent verdict remain (3 and 2). Potential silent-wrong rows: 0 on both seeds (seed 71 had 5). Closing the gate needs Contract rulings (chamfer corners at vertices whose faces are not mutually perpendicular, blends that run into another feature, rule 4 for plane-sphere blends and shell offsets, faces used up by a shell's offsets, values past a face's width that OCCT builds) and Forge capability (trimmed blends around another feature, NURBS cross-hole blends, three-blend D-flat corners, two-edge corners of mixed convexity, shells of mitred blends). Regenerate: BLEND_BATCH_OUT=blend<seed>.jsonl BLEND_SEED=<seed> BLEND_COUNT=400 BLEND_CURVED=60 BLEND_SEQ=100 BLEND_ADV=120 cargo test --release -p forge-blend --test oracle_batch write_blend_oracle_batch -- --ignored (about 80 s per seed); then, from oracle/, uv run python ../forge/crates/forge-blend/oracle/occt_blend_diff.py blend<seed>.jsonl --reference-all --out report.json --expect ../forge/crates/forge-blend/oracle/expected-summary.json --seed <seed> (exit status non-zero when a pinned field differs or the gate fails; about 12 min per seed). Deliberate update from the round-5 pin, with the reasons: (1) Forge refuses a corner of three chamfers at a vertex whose faces are not mutually perpendicular (SPEC §8.3 rule 3's test, |n_i . n_j| <= ANGULAR_TOLERANCE) with CHAMFER_FAILED naming the vertex: SPEC §6.7 defines no chamfer corner, and OCCT's differs from Forge's corner triangle there (up to 2.35e-3 of the volume on seed 71, the 5 METRIC_DIFF rows); on seed 17 six such rows had agreed within rule 5's 1e-5 only because the chamfers were small against the body (4 NORMALIZED, 2 MATCH), so Forge's valid count drops 558 -> 552 there, and seed 71's five potential silent-wrong rows become OCCT_ONLY (549 unchanged); the script counts these refusals as needing a Contract ruling (`gap_kind`: a *_FAILED whose reason says it awaits a Contract ruling); (2) a blend that runs into another feature of the body (a hole's or boss's rim inside a face, a tunnel, a drill point, a void) is FILLET_FAILED / CHAMFER_FAILED naming the obstacle's face, with the value that builds clear of it in the reason, instead of *_TOO_LARGE (SPEC §6.6 defines the rolling ball there): 7 and 13 OCCT_ONLY rows move from `needs_ruling` to `needs_capability` (OCCT's body equals the exact trimmed rolling-ball reference in 2 and 2 of them and differs from it by up to 1.1e-4 and 2.4e-4 in 5 and 11: evidence for the Contract ruling, in `occt_vs_reference` per row), and their `at_max` checks go (seed 17: 80 -> 60 rows; seed 71: 61 now); (3) the script applies rule 4 with the SPEC's named constants (ANGULAR_TOLERANCE, LINEAR_TOLERANCE) and reports a plane-sphere chamfer whose only difference is the bevel's boundary edges as RULE4_OUTSIDE_SPEC_TEXT instead of RULE4_EDGES (3 and 2 rows; COUNT_DIFF either way, the gate numbers do not change), and decides perpendicular corners with |a . b| <= ANGULAR_TOLERANCE (the cross-product form rounded to >= 1.0 in floating point); (4) Forge's other round-6 changes (shells of collapsing cavities are SHELL_THICKNESS_TOO_LARGE with the collapse thickness as a confirmed candidate; well-conditioned closest points for nearly parallel lines; the search from astronomically large values; face names and widths in messages) change no row of either seed.
